weekly: Course Mechanics & Syllabus Review: Overview of the course structure, expectations, assessment methods, and major themes in neuroscience.
A Brief History of Neuroscience: Introduction to major discoveries, ideas, and figures that shaped the scientific study of the brain and nervous system
Research Methods in Neuroscience: Introduction to methods used to investigate brain structure, function, and behavior, including experimental and neuroimaging techniques
Structure and Function of Neurons: Examination of neurons, their structure and electrical activity, and how neurons communicate with one another.
Evolution of the Human Brain: Examination of how the brain evolved and how changes in brain structure and organization relate to human cognition and behavior.
Neuroscience of Sensation and Perception: Examination of how the nervous system detects, processes, and interprets sensory information from the environment and the body
Neuroscience of Attention: Examination of the neural mechanisms that allow us to select, prioritize, and maintain focus on relevant information
Neuroscience of Learning and Memory: Examination of the neural mechanisms underlying learning, memory formation, storage, retrieval, and consolidation.
Neuroscience of Emotions: Examination of the neural systems involved in emotional processing, including the generation, regulation, and expression of emotions.
Neuroscience of Concept Formation, Categorization, and Knowledge: Examination of how the brain organizes information into concepts and categories and builds and uses stored knowledge.
Neuroscience of Language: Examination of the neural systems underlying language comprehension, production, representation, and communication.
Neuroscience of Judgment, Decision-Making, and Reasoning: Examination of the neural processes involved in evaluating information, making decisions, solving problems, and drawing conclusions.
Neuroscience of Consciousness: Examination of the neural basis of conscious experience, including awareness, subjective experience, and different states of consciousness
